items.title: The Ten Causes Regrouped Once More: Desirable, Undesirable, Augmenting, Cyclic, and Liberating

items.zh: 又建立因有五種相。一、可愛因，二、不可愛因，三、增長因，四、流轉因，五、還滅因。
items.en: Further, cause, when established, has five further marks: first, the desirable cause; second, the undesirable cause; third, the augmenting cause; fourth, the cause of cyclic existence; fifth, the cause of cessation.

items.title: The Seven Marks a Cause Must Have to Actually Function as a Cause

items.zh: 又建立因有七種相。謂無常法是因，無有常法能為法因。謂或為生因，或為得因，或為成立因，或為成辦因，或為作用因。又雖無常法為無常法因，然與他性為因，亦與後自性為因，非即此剎那。
items.en: Further, cause, when established, has seven marks. First: only an impermanent phenomenon can be a cause; no permanent phenomenon can ever be the cause of anything — whether as the cause of arising, of attainment, of establishment, of completion, or of function. Second: although it is an impermanent phenomenon that serves as the cause of an impermanent phenomenon, it does so both as a cause for a differing nature and as a cause for its own later nature — though not within that very same instant.

items.zh: 又雖與他性為因，及與後自性為因，然已生未滅方能為因，非未生已滅。又雖已生未滅，然得餘緣方能為因，非不得餘緣。又雖得餘緣，然成變異方能為因，非未變異。
items.en: Third: although it serves as a cause for a differing nature and as a cause for its own later nature, only what has already arisen and not yet ceased can serve as a cause — not what has not yet arisen, nor what has already ceased. Fourth: although already arisen and not yet ceased, only that which has obtained its remaining conditions can serve as a cause — not that which has not obtained them. Fifth: although its remaining conditions have been obtained, only that which has undergone transformation can serve as a cause — not that which has not yet undergone transformation.

items.zh: 又雖成變異，必與功能相應，方能為因，非失功能。又雖與功能相應，然必相稱相順方能為因，非不相稱相順。由如是七種相，隨其所應，諸因建立應知。
items.en: Sixth: although it has undergone transformation, only what still corresponds to its own capacity can serve as a cause — not what has lost that capacity. Seventh: although it corresponds to its own capacity, only what is truly commensurate and concordant with a result can serve as its cause — not what is neither commensurate nor concordant. It is by these seven marks, each applied as is fitting, that the establishment of causes in every case should be understood.

items.title: A New Topic Opens: Marks Establishment, and the Sevenfold Outline of Thought

items.zh: 云何相施設建立？嗢拕南曰：體、所緣、行相、等起、與差別、決擇、及流轉，略辯相應知。應知此相略有七種。一、體性，二、所緣，三、行相，四、等起，五、差別，六、決擇，七、流轉。
items.en: Further, how is marks establishment to be understood? A summary verse states: nature, object, mode of activity, arising-together, and difference, determination, and circulation — stated briefly, this should be understood as their mark. It should be known that this mark comprises, briefly, seven kinds: first, nature; second, object; third, mode of activity; fourth, arising-together; fifth, difference; sixth, determination; seventh, circulation.

items.title: What Applied and Sustained Thought Actually Are

items.zh: 尋伺體性者，謂不深推度所緣，思為體性。若深推度所緣，慧為體性應知。尋伺所緣者，謂依名身、句身、文身，義為所緣。
items.en: As for the nature of applied and sustained thought: when there is no deep investigation into the object, volition is their nature. When there is deep investigation into the object, it should be understood that discernment is their nature. As for their object: it is the meaning as conveyed through a body of names, a body of phrases, and a body of letters, that serves as their object.

items.zh: 尋伺行相者，謂即於此所緣，尋求行相，是尋；即於此所緣，伺察行相，是伺。
items.en: As for their mode of activity: with respect to this same object, the mode of activity that seeks it out is applied thought; the mode of activity that examines it closely is sustained thought.

items.title: How Thought Gives Rise to Speech, Its Differences, and How It Relates to Ordinary Discrimination

items.zh: 尋伺等起者，謂發起語言。尋伺差別者，有七種差別。謂有相、無相，乃至不染污，如前說。
items.en: As for their arising-together: it is the giving rise to speech. As for their differences: there are seven kinds of difference — namely, with characteristic and without characteristic, and so on up through undefiled, exactly as explained previously.

items.zh: 尋伺決擇者，若尋伺即分別耶？設分別即尋伺耶？謂諸尋伺必是分別，或有分別非尋伺。謂望出世智，所餘一切三界心心所皆是分別，而非尋伺。
items.en: As for their determination: is applied and sustained thought simply discrimination? Or is discrimination simply applied and sustained thought? It should be understood that applied and sustained thought are necessarily a form of discrimination, but there is discrimination that is not applied and sustained thought. That is: measured against uncontaminated wisdom, every remaining mental phenomenon throughout the three realms is discrimination, and is not applied and sustained thought.

items.zh: 尋伺流轉者，若那落迦尋伺，何等行？何所觸？何所引？何相應？何所求？何業轉耶？如那落迦，如是傍生、餓鬼、人、欲界天、初靜慮地天所有尋伺，何等行？何所觸？何所引？何相應？何所求？何業轉耶？

items.title: Circulation: The Same Craving-Driven Mind, Realm by Realm — and Marks Establishment Closes

items.zh: 謂那落迦尋伺，唯是慼行，觸非愛境，引發於苦，與憂相應，常求脫苦，嬈心業轉。如那落迦尋伺一向受苦，餓鬼尋伺亦爾。傍生、人趣、大力餓鬼所有尋伺，多分慼行，少分欣行；多分觸非愛境，少分觸可愛境；多分引苦，少分引樂；多分憂相應，少分喜相應；多分求脫苦，少分求遇樂；嬈心業轉。
items.en: As for the hell-beings' applied and sustained thought: it is entirely a distressed activity, coming into contact only with disagreeable objects, giving rise only to suffering, associated with grief, forever seeking to escape suffering, its activity a ceaseless mental agitation. As with the hell-beings' thought, wholly given to suffering, so too the hungry ghosts'. As for animals, humans, and powerful ghosts: their thought is for the most part distressed, only occasionally joyful; for the most part in contact with disagreeable objects, only occasionally with agreeable ones; for the most part giving rise to suffering, only occasionally to pleasure; for the most part associated with grief, only occasionally with joy; for the most part seeking to escape suffering, only occasionally to encounter pleasure — its activity still a mental agitation.

items.zh: 欲界諸天所有尋伺，多分欣行，少分慼行；多分觸可愛境，少分觸非愛境；多分引樂，少分引苦；多分喜相應，少分憂相應；多分求遇樂，少分求脫苦；嬈心業轉。初靜慮地天所有尋伺，一向欣行，一向觸內可愛境界，一向引樂，一向喜相應，唯求不離樂，不嬈心業轉。
items.en: As for the desire realm's gods: their thought is for the most part joyful, only occasionally distressed; for the most part in contact with agreeable objects, only occasionally disagreeable ones; for the most part giving rise to pleasure, only occasionally suffering; for the most part associated with joy, only occasionally grief; for the most part seeking to encounter pleasure, only occasionally to escape suffering — its activity still a mental agitation. As for the first dhyāna's gods: their thought is entirely joyful, entirely in contact with an inward, agreeable object, entirely giving rise to pleasure, entirely associated with joy, seeking only never to be parted from that pleasure — its activity is no longer a mental agitation at all.

items.title: A Third Gateway Opens: Sound Reasoning Attention, and Its Eightfold Outline

items.zh: 云何如理作意施設建立？嗢拕南曰：依處、及與事、求、受用、正行、二菩提資糧、到彼岸方便。應知建立略由八相。謂由依處故、事故、求故、受用故、正行故、聲聞乘資糧方便故、獨覺乘資糧方便故、波羅蜜多引發方便故。
items.en: Further, how is the establishment of sound reasoning attention to be understood? A summary verse states: locus, and also its matters, seeking, and enjoyment, correct conduct, the two vehicles' provisions for awakening, and the means of reaching the far shore. It should be known that this establishment comprises, briefly, eight marks: through locus, through its matters, through seeking, through enjoyment, through correct conduct, through the means of provisioning the śrāvaka vehicle, through the means of provisioning the pratyekabuddha vehicle, and through the means of drawing forth the perfections.

items.title: Six Occasions Where Sound Reasoning Meets Wholesome Mind-States

items.zh: 如理作意相應尋伺依處者，謂有六種依處。一、決定時，二、止息時，三、作業時，四、世間離欲時，五、出世離欲時，六、攝益有情時。
items.en: As for the loci of applied and sustained thought associated with sound reasoning attention: there are six such loci. First, the time of resolve; second, the time of putting evil to rest; third, the time of wholesome action; fourth, the time of worldly freedom from desire; fifth, the time of transcendent freedom from desire; sixth, the time of benefiting beings.

items.title: Eight Kinds of Accomplishment Sound Reasoning Produces

items.zh: 如理作意相應尋伺事者，謂八種事。一、施所成福作用事，二、戒所成福作用事，三、修所成福作用事，四、聞所成事，五、思所成事，六、餘修所成事，七、簡擇所成事，八、攝益有情所成事。
items.en: As for the matters accomplished by applied and sustained thought associated with sound reasoning attention: there are eight such matters. First, the merit accomplished through generosity; second, the merit accomplished through moral precepts; third, the merit accomplished through cultivation; fourth, the matter accomplished through hearing; fifth, the matter accomplished through reflection; sixth, the further matter accomplished through cultivation; seventh, the matter accomplished through discernment; eighth, the matter accomplished for the benefit of beings.

blocks.text: Today closes the account of causation with two important ideas, a grouping of causes by where they lead and seven marks of any true cause, and then moves to the second and third gateways of the three grounds of thought: the **marks** of applied and sustained thought, and **sound reasoning attention** (如理作意).

One passage is untranslated (0302c04–c09): a series of questions about thought in each realm, "of what kind is the thought of hell-beings? what does it contact? what draws it? with what does it correspond? what does it seek? what karma does it carry out?", repeated for animals, ghosts, humans, the desire gods, and the first dhyāna.

subs.head: Causes grouped by where they lead

blocks.text: The ten causes are regrouped as desirable, undesirable, augmenting, cyclic (leading round in saṃsāra), and liberating. Venerable Miào Jìng's image: dreaming. Good and bad dreams are both unreal, yet we prefer good ones; the liberating cause is waking from the dream through discipline, concentration, and wisdom.
A cause must have seven marks:

items: It is **impermanent**: "no permanent phenomenon can ever be the cause of anything."
It produces something other than itself, and its own later continuation.
It must meet the right conditions.
It must be present when it acts.
It must have **undergone transformation**, that is, ripened. Venerable Miào Jìng: "if you need ten thousand degrees of calm-and-insight power to reach the first dhyāna, five thousand won't do."
It must **retain its capacity**. Venerable Miào Jìng: roast a grain in a pan and it is no longer a seed, "so before the result ripens, whatever wrong you have done, repent quickly."
It must be **commensurate and concordant**: "plant melons, get melons; plant beans, get beans."

blocks.text: Both teachers compare these with the "six meanings of seeds" in the *Mahāyānasaṃgraha* and the *Cheng Weishi Lun*: momentary, simultaneous with its result, continuous, determinate, dependent on conditions, and producing its own result. The first mark is the philosophical point: whatever really causes must itself change. Hence, as on Day 19, a permanent cause of the world is ruled out.
The second gateway describes applied and sustained thought under seven headings: nature, object, mode of activity, arising-together, difference, determination, and circulation.

items: **Nature**: "When there is no deep investigation into the object, volition is their nature. When there is deep investigation, discernment (wisdom) is their nature." Thought is volition when it is casual and wisdom when it is careful.
**Object**: the meaning carried by names, phrases, and letters. Venerable Miào Jìng: "all evils" alone is not a phrase; "do no evil" is.

**Determination**: "applied and sustained thought are necessarily discrimination, but there is discrimination that is not." Master Cháng Bǎi: thought is always a kind of discrimination, but higher meditative states still discriminate without applied or sustained thought.

blocks.text: The last heading follows thought through the realms. From the hells to the desire heavens, thought proceeds with "agitated mind" (嬈心). Venerable Miào Jìng: 嬈 means "an uneasy mind … with desire the mind keeps grasping outward". In the first dhyāna it does not, since its gods, content with their bliss, are calm. Ru-Yi's "mental burning" for 嬈 is stronger than the teachers' reading.

The third gateway is **sound reasoning attention** (如理作意), attention in accordance with truth, which we have met since Day 2 as the point where an ordinary being can become noble. It has eight marks: locus, matters, seeking, enjoyment, correct conduct, and provisions for the three vehicles.

Its six loci are occasions where it meets wholesome states: the time of resolve, of putting to rest, and so on. Both teachers map them onto the eleven wholesome mental factors: resolve is faith; benefiting beings is non-harm. Venerable Miào Jìng's image for the non-attachment it brings: with glue on your hands, everything you touch sticks; without it, you touch things and nothing sticks.

quiz.q: The text regroups the causes as desirable, undesirable, augmenting, cyclic, and liberating. What image does Venerable Miào Jìng use?
options: dreaming: good and bad dreams are both unreal, yet one prefers good ones; the liberating cause is waking from the dream through discipline, concentration, and wisdom
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: "Like dreaming — a good dream or a bad one, both unreal … yet one would rather have a good one"; the liberating cause "is Buddhists studying the Dharma to stop dreaming — to wake up — training in discipline, concentration, and wisdom." Desirable and undesirable causes moistened by craving become augmenting causes. Master Cháng Bǎi: without cutting affliction completely, every result still turns in saṃsāra.

quiz.q: The text says causes have seven marks. What is the first?
options: only impermanent phenomena can be causes; nothing permanent can cause anything
quiz.why: "Only an impermanent phenomenon can be a cause; no permanent phenomenon can ever be the cause of anything." In order: impermanence; causing another nature and its own later nature (not in the same instant); already arisen and not yet ceased; obtaining other conditions; having undergone transformation; retaining capacity; being commensurate and concordant. A, C, D are the third, fourth, and seventh.

quiz.q: The fifth mark: only what "has undergone transformation" can be a cause. What image does Venerable Miào Jìng use?
options: transformation means ripening — if it takes ten thousand degrees of calm and insight to reach the first dhyāna, five thousand won't do
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: "'Transformation' means ripening — if it is raw and unripe, not yet mature"; "if you need ten thousand degrees of calm-and-insight power to reach the first dhyāna, five thousand won't do." Master Cháng Bǎi: attaining concentration takes long practice and cultivation. The translation renders it literally as "undergone transformation."

quiz.q: The sixth mark: a cause must retain its capacity. What example does Venerable Miào Jìng give, and what does he urge?
options: older seeds are better; save seeds
grain roasted in a pan can no longer sprout; so before a misdeed ripens, repent at once
more capacity is better; do more
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: "Take a grain of rice or wheat — it is a seed, but roast it in a pan and it can no longer be a seed"; "so before the result ripens, whatever wrong you have done, repent quickly." Repentance is like roasting the seed of bad karma. Master Cháng Bǎi cites the *Pixunji*: a seed kept dry still is a seed; only fire destroys it as one.

quiz.q: According to the treatise, what seven kinds make up the marks of applied and sustained thought?
options: number, place, measure, lifespan, enjoyment, birth, own body
nature, object, mode of activity, arising-together, difference, determination, circulation
the seven marks of a cause
quiz.why: "First, nature; second, object; third, mode of activity; fourth, arising-together; fifth, difference; sixth, determination; seventh, circulation." Master Cháng Bǎi: these describe applied and sustained thought by whether beings of the three realms have it, while also distinguishing the realms. A is the realm establishment begun in fascicle 4.

quiz.q: According to the treatise, what is the nature of applied and sustained thought?
options: volition, when not investigating deeply; discernment, when investigating deeply
quiz.why: "When there is no deep investigation into the object, volition is their nature. When there is deep investigation into the object, it should be understood that discernment is their nature." Master Cháng Bǎi: "Without deep reflection and inference on the object, it is mostly the factor of volition." Venerable Miào Jìng: "not investigating deeply" is like doing something in a rush.

quiz.q: Under "determination": "applied and sustained thought are necessarily discrimination, but there is discrimination that is not." How do the teachers explain this?
options: thought is always discrimination, but not vice versa — measured against transcendent wisdom, all mind in the three realms is discrimination; discrimination without the craving for thought is not thought
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: "All applied and sustained thought is discrimination; not all discrimination is such thought" — the intermediate dhyāna has only sustained thought and the second dhyāna up has neither, yet discrimination remains. Venerable Miào Jìng: some discrimination is not thought "because there is no craving for thought"; citing the *Great Treatise on the Perfection of Wisdom*, sages of the eighth ground and above speak without discrimination. Note the translation softens 皆是分別而非尋伺 to "yet not all of it is."
